intro: How to use this workbook: what is inside, what the evidence labels mean, and the safety rules.
Start at the top. The CONTENTS list links to every tab; run one drill at a time.

blocks.title: What This Is
blocks.text: One workbook that collects evidence-based self-improvement knowledge in sixteen tabs. Each row shows what the science says, how strong the evidence is, and one practice you can try. The goal is honest guidance, not hype.

blocks.title: How to Use It
blocks.text: Read this page first. Pick the tab where you are weakest and start there, or work through the tabs in order. Run one 1-week drill at a time from that tab. When you want a full plan, use ACTION_PLAN and follow the 12-week program.

blocks.title: Scenario Tabs
blocks.text: Six tabs answer the question 'what do I actually say?' Each row shows the common mistake, what to do instead, exact words, why it works, and a one-week drill. Start with the situation you avoid most, not the one that looks most impressive.

blocks.title: Find Your Weak Spot
blocks.text:
I freeze when I have to speak up -> SCENARIOS
I run out of things to say -> SCENARIOS and DATING
I cannot tell if someone is interested -> DATING
People ask me to repeat myself -> VOICE & SPEECH
My voice sounds thin or rushed -> VOICE & SPEECH
I slouch and hide in photos -> PRESENCE & STYLE
I do not know what colours suit me -> PRESENCE & STYLE
I say yes and then resent it -> SELF & RESILIENCE
I spiral when criticised -> SELF & RESILIENCE
I misread the room -> SOCIAL AWARENESS
I do not know how to keep friends -> SOCIAL AWARENESS
I avoid hard conversations -> SCENARIOS and SELF & RESILIENCE

blocks.title: How to Run a Scenario
blocks.text: Pick one situation. Read the mistake and the steps. Say the lines out loud three times. Run the one-week drill. Then try it once for real at the easiest level. Review what happened without insulting yourself.

blocks.title: Evidence Legend
blocks.text: The label on each row tells you how much to trust it. Strong: many good studies agree. Moderate: several decent studies support it. Emerging: early or small studies hint at it. Mixed: studies disagree or the effect is small. Myth: good studies show it does not work.

blocks.title: The Rules
blocks.text: This knowledge is for building yourself and for defending against manipulation. There is no harm-playbook here; every dark tactic is shown with a counter you can use. Use what you learn to protect people, never to use them.

blocks.title: Safety & Limits
blocks.text: Nothing here is medical advice. If you feel depressed or anxious for weeks, see a doctor or a qualified professional. If a topic mentions drugs or treatments, see a doctor too. This workbook is a starting point, not a replacement for real care.

blocks.title: How to Get Results
blocks.text: Practice volume beats reading every time; two minutes daily beats two hours once. Small steps repeated are what change you. Track what you do in ACTION_PLAN so you can see your own progress.
